source_row.rationale: Elevated bilirubin, causing jaundice, can result from various underlying mechanisms, including increased red blood cell breakdown/hemolysis (increasing bilirubin production), impaired liver processing/conjugation of bilirubin (such as in certain liver diseases), or obstruction of bile flow (such as from gallstones or a tumor blocking the bile duct) — requiring further evaluation, often including fractionated bilirubin levels (direct/indirect) and additional testing, to determine the specific underlying cause.
source_row.source_name: Clinical Laboratory Reference Standards — Bilirubin and Jaundice Differential
source_row.stem: A client presents with yellowing of the skin and sclera, and lab work reveals a significantly elevated bilirubin level, and a family member assumes this kind of finding only ever applies to newborn babies and has no relevance for an adult client.
